description: A securities finance director must authorize a reinvestment plan for cash collateral received on securities loans and set the permitted instruments, reserve, allocation, maturity, and monitoring conditions, with input from counterparty risk, compliance, client coverage, and investment operations.

shared_context.S1: The desk currently holds $25,000,000 of cash collateral received from securities-lending transactions.
shared_context.S2: The draft plan would invest the full $25,000,000 in 30-day commercial paper issued by Delta Financial.
shared_context.S3: Mara makes the binding decision on the collateral reinvestment plan.
shared_context.S4: The desk's daily pre-trade huddle includes a one-minute exception report from counterparty risk, compliance, client coverage, and investment operations before the final authorization.

PF1.text: Jonas confirmed in a counterparty review completed this morning that Delta Financial's commercial paper is under active rating review; until the review closes, desk policy prohibits any new purchase of Delta commercial paper. Jonas recorded the result in his working file, but the counterparty system has not been updated yet.

PF2.text: Elena found this week in the applicable collateral-investment mandate that the cash may be placed only in government Treasury bills or AAA-rated bank certificates of deposit, each with a maturity of no more than 14 days; the restriction has not yet been added to the desk's pre-trade checklist.

PF3.text: Ravi received a client instruction confirmed by email this morning requiring $7,000,000 of this collateral pool to remain uninvested cash because the client expects a possible securities-loan recall; he has not yet attached the email to the reinvestment ticket.

PF4.text: Nora confirmed with the settlement team today that the platform can process exactly $12,000,000 of Treasury bills and $6,000,000 of AAA bank certificates of deposit on a T+1 basis, with daily position reconciliation; this capacity confirmation is in an operations note that has not yet been circulated.

acceptance_conditions: The reinvestment plan must be approved.
Exactly $7,000,000 must remain as uninvested cash.
Exactly $12,000,000 must be allocated to Treasury bills and exactly $6,000,000 to AAA-rated bank certificates of deposit.
No amount may be allocated to Delta Financial commercial paper.
The maximum maturity must be exactly 14 days or less.
Settlement must be set for T+1 and daily position reconciliation must be required.
The plan must include commitments for the $7,000,000 cash reserve and daily position reconciliation.
The Delta Financial rating-review fact must be cited as justification.

content_checks.C7: any(c['type'] == 'cash_reserve' for c in commitments) and any(c['type'] == 'daily_reconciliation' for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The draft assigns all collateral to Delta Financial commercial paper, while PF1 changes delta_financial_cp_allocation_usd from the proposed positive amount to exactly 0 and supplies the required rating-review basis.
The draft uses 30-day commercial paper, while PF2 changes the permitted instrument set to Treasury bills or AAA bank certificates of deposit and changes maximum_maturity_days to no more than 14.
Without PF3 the draft invests all $25,000,000, but PF3 changes uninvested_cash_reserve_usd to exactly $7,000,000 and leaves exactly $18,000,000 available for an approvable reinvestment plan.

Without PF4 the settlement would lack a confirmed executable allocation, while PF4 changes the operational plan to exactly $12,000,000 of Treasury bills and $6,000,000 of bank CDs settled in one day and requires daily reconciliation.
